newsitem.title: UK: U.S. cold keeps oil price bubbling near 6-year high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cold keeps oil price bubbling near 6-year high.

text.p: Oil prices stayed in sight of six-year highs on Monday, fending off modest losses at the end of last week amid renewed United States heating oil demand.
North Sea Brent crude oil futures traded in London rose 17 cents to $24.51 a barrel at 1530 GMT, not far off the $25.06 post Gulf War high set in October last year.
Dealers said there was still a reluctance in the market to risk selling oil while winter temperatures in key European or U.S. consumer regions kept demand buoyant and inventories low.
"Everyone is afraid to sell it," said Jeff Potter, managing director of brokers Univest Ireland in Dublin.

Private forecaster Weather Services Corp said it expected below normal temperatures at least until midweek in the Northeast U.S., the world's largest heating oil consuming region, followed by another cold spell later this week.
" The cold weather in the U.S. is certainly helping," said a London-based trader. "Europe has been lulled into a false sense of security because of the milder weather here."
Record low inventory levels in the U.S. and Europe have kept a flame under oil prices over recent weeks but signs from the latest European data were that stock levels were on the rebound.
Inventories in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 13.51 million barrels in December to 1.034 billion barrels, Stichting Euroilstock said in a monthly report released on Monday.
The lean stock situation, a result of oil company tactics to slim down stockpiles to cut costs and free up capital for investments, remains key to the oil price outlook.
"If stocks are really on the rebound then there has to be a good chance this market will come off, possibly quite heavily, at some point," said a London trader. "But it may a be while yet."
